component: P16 bounded inbox accounting and concurrent payload assurance
constraints: Synchronous process-local queue: at most sixteen entries and one MiB retained bytes, sixty-second caller-clock lifetime, per-peer count limits and all-entry expiry.
Compound operations need one atomic accounting decision; immutable exact byte payloads, no background service, scheduler or disk/network persistence.
alternatives: Python native deque with explicit lock around compound accounting.
Rust Crossbeam bounded channels plus byte/peer/expiry accounting.
C#/F# bounded Channels with explicit overflow behavior and compound accounting.
Erlang/Elixir process isolation and mailboxes with separate bounded admission.
rationale: KEEP explicit locked accounting: count-bounded channels or mailboxes alone do not enforce aggregate bytes, per-peer limits and expiry behind a live head. Alternatives remain credible for changed deployment constraints; no performance winner is established here.

FIX assurance coverage: identical producer bytes allowed returned-payload substitution to survive the concurrency test. Sixteen distinct synthetic bytes and admitted-versus-dequeued multiset equality detect that substitution.
